title: Ref safety follow-up: reject % outright, and decide the write-side question
description:
Follow-up required by TASK-185's AC5 and its LOW-1, both recorded at close. Two related items on the same control.

**Item 1 — the percent-encoding defense is narrower than the docs that ship with it (LOW-1).**

`UNSAFE_REF_RE` matches only the literal token `%2e%2e`. The TASK-185 reviewer executed the committed guard against adjacent forms and found these pass through:

```
"%252e%252e/x"             (double-encoded)
"..%2fx"  "..%5cx"         (literal .. with an encoded separator)
"..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd"
"x%2f..%2fetc"
"....//etc/passwd"         (naive ../-stripper bait)
"a%00/etc/passwd"
```

None is exploitable today: every one needs a consumer that percent-decodes or naively strips `../` BEFORE resolving, and no such consumer exists — agents open a ref as a literal repo-relative path. That is why it closed as LOW rather than blocking.

The part that does matter is the overclaim. `skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md:997` and the `kb_graph_query` tool description at `src/mcp-server.js:550` both tell agents the guard covers refs "disguised via ... percent-encoding" with no qualification. False confidence in a control is the exact failure class this repo keeps paying for.

**Recommended fix (from the reviewer, and it is a good one): reject any ref containing `%` outright.** Evidence it is safe: the reviewer ran all 225 refs currently in `knowledge/graph/graph.json` through the guard and **zero contain a `%`**. So the false-negative cost is provably zero today, and it replaces a token blacklist — which loses arms races by construction — with a whitelist-shaped rule. If that is adopted, the docs become true rather than needing softening.

**Item 2 — the write side (TASK-185 AC5's deferred question).**

`GRAPH_SCHEMA` in `src/knowledge-graph.js` has `ref: {type: 'string', minLength: 1}` and validates no shape, so an unsafe ref can still be WRITTEN into `knowledge/graph/graph.json`. It simply will not be surfaced by `kb_graph_query`.

The TASK-185 reviewer assessed this as **correctly scoped out and NOT a weakness**, with reasoning worth preserving: `safeRef` sits at the point of consumption — the only place a ref becomes an instruction to open a file — so the control is complete regardless of what is stored. Schema hardening would be defense-in-depth, would be a genuine trust-boundary change, and **would break existing graphs at load time**.

So this ticket must not assume the write side needs hardening. Decide it deliberately: either add write-side validation with a migration path for the existing 225-node graph, or record an explicit decision that consumption-point validation is the right and sufficient boundary. Both are legitimate outcomes; an undecided residual is not.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first demonstrates the current residuals: '..%2fx', '..%5cx', '%252e%252e/x' and '....//etc/passwd' currently pass through safeRef unchanged. Capture the red-run output verbatim as the tests-first evidence.

Item 1 is resolved by a rule that does not lose an arms race. If the recommended '%'-rejection is adopted, first re-verify against the CURRENT knowledge/graph/graph.json that zero live refs contain '%' (the 225-ref figure is from 2026-08-02 and the graph grows every close) — do not rely on the recorded number.

The docs stop overclaiming: skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md and the kb_graph_query tool description describe exactly what the guard does and does not cover. Both SKILL.md parity copies byte-identical.

Item 2 is DECIDED and the decision recorded in the closing comment: either write-side validation lands with a proven migration path for the existing graph, or an explicit reasoned decision that consumption-point validation is the sufficient boundary. An undecided residual is not an acceptable close.

If write-side validation IS adopted, prove it does not break the existing graph at load time — run the real knowledge/graph/graph.json through the new schema and show the result. This is the specific risk the TASK-185 reviewer flagged.
No regression in false-negative behaviour: every ref in the live graph must still pass through unchanged after the fix. Show the count.
npm run test:all is green; dist/mcp-server.cjs rebuilt via npm run build:plugin and committed, with tests/e2e/dist-parity.spec.js passing.
